en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation and Offerings of the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful King Ārya-Hayagrīva,
Establishing Great Spiritual Efficacy, Volume One: By the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery,
Tejin and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
I take refuge in Vajrapāṇi, the Great Bodhisattva, Lord of Secrets,
who can expound the Supreme Vehicle and cause one to swiftly realize awakening—
haya-hrīḥ-va— able to destroy all demonic obstacles.
Through the skillful means of compassion, he manifests as a great wrathful form,
a sun-disk of great majesty; by illuminating the darkness of the infinite realms of practitioners,
he causes them to swiftly attain siddhi.
Flowing with the water of ambrosia, it washes away the various seeds of habitual tendencies within the *ālayavijñāna*;
swiftly gathering the accumulations of merit and wisdom, one attains the perfectly pure *dharmakāya*. Therefore, I prostrate in homage.
Now, relying upon the secret mantras and the teachings of the subtle *naya*,
I shall explain the most secret ritual manual. First,
the *ācārya* should select a disciple for the practice of secret mantras who possesses pure faith in the Three Jewels.
Loving and revering the Mahāyāna, thirsting for and aspiring to the Yoga teachings,
they delight in practicing the bodhisattva conduct;
their minds are not timid or weak as they seek to study the gateway of correspondence, relinquishing body, life, and wealth.
Free from weariness and stinginess, born of noble lineage and endowed with all faculties,
learned and guardians of the True Dharma; delighting in the practice of the six perfections,
they compassionately regard all sentient beings and are ever clad in the great armor of their vows.
To fully deliver all classes of sentient beings throughout boundless realms and cause them to swiftly realize awakening—
if an ācārya sees such a person who is a vessel for the Dharma, he should skillfully exhort and guide them.
First, one should expound for them the subtle path to enlightenment and the skillful principles of Prajñāpāramitā; then,
swiftly bestow upon them the path to awakening by granting the three refuges and causing them to resolve upon bodhicitta.
Next, one bestows the three types of unimpeded bodhisattva vows pertaining to the three times;
only then does one lead them into the maṇḍala,
confer the empowerment of their own chosen deity, and grant the vidyādhara protection.
One should show the maṇḍala and proclaim the samaya:
"From now until the attainment of Buddhahood, do not abandon the bodhicitta;
revere the ācārya as equal to all Buddhas."
Just like Vajrapāṇi, one should maintain deep respect for all fellow practitioners and never treat them with contempt;
having received the vajra and the vajra-gong from the teacher, one does so for the sake of seeking siddhi.

Until reaching the site of enlightenment, one should never abandon the face-to-face empowerment master who has bestowed the complete instructions of the tutelary deity with certainty and without error;
thereafter, one should practice with courageous diligence.
The practitioner of yoga,
having received the ritual manual of the tutelary deity from the master,
should go to a secluded place.
Alternatively, one may establish a pure chamber in a mountain forest, a secluded valley, or any other superior location described in the various teachings;
or one may prepare the ground in a vihāra,
smearing it with cow dung.
Furthermore, smear the site of practice (maṇḍala) with white sandalwood paste;
hang banners all around it and place a celestial canopy above.
To the west of the altar, install the image of the Principal Deity (bimba).
The practitioner faces the image at the eastern side of the maṇḍala,
spreading a mat of *kuśa* grass as a seat,
or sitting upon a small stool with legs covered by a cloth.
Arrange the various positions of the noble ones within the distributed maṇḍala.
Place two *arghas* filled with fragrant water and set four auspicious vases (*kalaśas*) at the four corners of the altar.
Every day, take various seasonal flowers and scatter them upon the altar.
Burn incense, apply fragrant ointments, and offer lamps, food, drink, and fruit.
Empower these offerings and distribute them around the four sides as an act of worship.
Arrange the offerings and decorations according to one's means;
each time entering the maṇḍala, prostrate with sincere devotion,
confess and repent, rejoice in merit, entreat [the Buddhas], dedicate the merit, and make vows.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"There is the Great Terrifying King, the Noble Hayagrīva.
I shall now speak of his heart-mantra and the sublime mudrā."
The entire great assembly has now gathered here.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva again addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Good son, listen attentively! The Tathāgatas of Boundless Power and Prowess, who are as boundless as space, have all served this Great King of Wrathful Majesty.
Furthermore, so too have the Tathāgatas of the past, numbering incalculable koṭis."
All have received his instruction and attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Immeasurable devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings constantly make offerings, pay homage, and serve him.
If one merely recollects this King of Wrathful Power,
it will cause all those who create obstacles and difficulties to be utterly destroyed;
no obstructors will dare to approach.
One should always remain far removed from such places.
Within a forty-li radius of where a practitioner dwells,
there shall be no demonic activities nor any malevolent spirits and ghosts.
He dwelt together with the great bodhisattvas. Then,
the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi arose from samādhi and,
having alerted them, summoned all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas,
asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all classes of living beings.
They all gather together;
furthermore, he extracts and gathers the various mentalities of those sentient beings.
Causing them to abide in a single essence within samādhi,
the fires that burn each of the world-systems— each numbering in the millions— are extinguished,
becoming only one great mass of fire.
Just as when the light of the seven suns shines,
the mouths of the great horses and other such streams all converge and are swallowed up,
until nothing remains but they are entirely transformed into fierce flames.
This is the sublime heart-mantra of the Noble Hayagrīva, the King of Great Wrathful Power;
it is like the mouth of a great horse that swallows and devours,
burning away all the various habitual tendencies and defiled minds within the ālayavijñāna of all sentient beings.
The supreme root mantra is proclaimed as follows:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām | tadyathā | julu julu | vijulu vijulu | gadāyakṣa | mahāvara | sarvavidyāvināyakān | bhaṭṭāram uccati | mṛtāya hūṃ phaṭ*. As soon as this sublime mantra is recited...
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
all Buddha-fields were scorched by the fiery light of the King of Great Wrathful Power,
becoming a single mass of blazing fire.
Mount Sumeru and Mahāsumeru,
the Iron Ring Mountains and the Great Iron Ring Mountains—
all the great oceans completely dry up.
It is completely incinerated, becoming ashes.
Such is the Samādhi of the Sublime Mind of the Noble Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.
The practitioner should always abide in the great bodhicitta and give rise to profound compassion.
Immediately, one directs the mind to visualize all Tathāgatas filling the entirety of space,
endowed with all the marks and signs of perfection, and all entered into the samādhi of the Dharma-realm.
Furthermore, one visualizes oneself abiding within the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas.
Then, one forms the seal that awakens all Tathāgatas:
with both hands, each making a vajra-fist,
the thumbs and middle fingers hook together.
Straighten and extend the two forefingers, with their sides touching each other.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajratiṣṭha hūṃ. Having bound this mudrā, recite the awakening mantra.
All Tathāgatas emerge from meditative absorption.
The practitioner of yoga should reflect thus and address the Buddhas:
"My body possesses little wisdom and little merit; I am submerged in the ocean of suffering."
I prostrate and beseech the majestic spiritual power of all Buddhas.
I pray only that you will not abandon your great compassionate original vow,
but out of compassion and pity, observe, protect, and mind me, delivering me from suffering.
Each of those Tathāgatas, by means of their supernatural powers,
empowers and protects the practitioner of yoga,
so that they may obtain an immeasurable accumulation of merit and mastery over body and mind.
Next, one should pay homage to the Tathāgatas of the four directions and request their protection.
First, one pays homage to all the Tathāgatas, beginning with the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the east;
the practitioner then prostrates with his entire body cast upon the ground.
Joining the two hands in the vajra-pañjali mudrā, extend them upward to the crown of the head;
placing the heart-mudrā upon the ground, pay homage with utmost sincerity.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ sarvatathāgata-pūjopasthānāyāntama-nir-yātaya me. Sarvatathāgata-vajrasattva-dhiṣṭhasvā-ma-hūṃ. Having bound the *śarīra-mudrā* (body-seal) and recited this mantra, one should present offerings and pay homage.
By performing this prostration,
the yogin shall constantly receive the empowerment of Vajrasattva until the attainment of Buddhahood.
May the bodhicitta be brought to perfection.
Next, prostrate to all Tathāgatas, beginning with the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava of the southern direction.
As before, stretch the body out and prostrate fully upon the ground.
Perform the vajra-añjali at the heart;
place the forehead upon the ground and pay homage with utmost sincerity.
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjābhiṣekāya taṃ namaḥ | niryātaya me | sarvatathāgatavajraratnābhiṣiñca māṃ | Tārā-uy-jeṣa. Because of offering worship and paying homage by forming the mudrā of surrendering the body and reciting this mantra.
Until they attain Buddhahood,
they shall constantly receive the empowerment from the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha throughout each stage.
Their merit will be perfected, and they will be endowed with all the primary and secondary marks of excellence.
One shall become the Dharma King of the three realms.
Next, prostrate to the Tathāgatas of the West, such as Amitāyus, and all other Tathāgatas.
As before, extend the body and place the vajra-palms joined at the crown of the head.
Placing one's mouth upon the ground, one performs a sincere and respectful prostration.
The mantra is as follows:

*Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjā-pratīcchana-tām anu-nir-ya-tā-maṃ hṛdaye*. Because of making this offering, reciting the mantra, and performing the prostration while sealing the body with the *śarīra-mudrā*, [one makes this offering].
Until they attain Buddhahood,
they shall always receive the empowerment of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
their wisdom will be perfected, and they will turn the sublime Wheel of Dharma.
Next, prostrate to all Tathāgatas, beginning with the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the northern direction.
Extending the body as before, place the vajra-palms at the heart and,
touching the crown of the head to the ground, pay homage with utmost sincerity.
The mantra is:

Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmaṇi ātmānaṃ niryātayāmi | Sarvatathāgata-vajrakarmakuru māṃ || (5) Because of offering, making offerings, prostrating, and revering by means of the mudrā of surrendering the body and reciting this mantra.
Until the attainment of Buddhahood,
one shall constantly receive the empowerment of the Bodhisattva Vajrakarma,
thereby accomplishing the vast karma of making offerings throughout all Buddha-worlds.
The practitioner then assumes the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*),
sits with the body upright and right mindfulness, keeping the limbs motionless.
With eyes closed in tranquil stillness, they enter into the contemplation of the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*).
Then, forming the seal of meditative concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*),
he first enters the meditative absorption of immeasurable loving-kindness (*maitrī-apramāṇa-samādhi*),
purifying his mind through compassion.
Universally taking as their object all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth,
they are all endowed with the Tathāgatagarbha and possess the threefold vajra of body, speech, and mind.
"By the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Having contemplated thus:
Then he recited the mantra of the Great Compassion Samādhi:
Oṃ mahāmaitrīya-sphara. Next, one should enter the wisdom of the samādhi of immeasurable compassion.
With a heart of compassion, one universally takes as objects all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth,
who are submerged in the ocean of suffering of saṃsāra and fail to awaken to their own minds.
By giving rise to false discrimination, they produce various afflictions and secondary afflictions;
therefore, they fail to realize that True Suchness is equal to space and transcends merits as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
"By the power of my cultivation of the empowerment of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Having visualized thus:
Then he recited the mantra of the Mahākaruṇā-samādhi:
Oṃ mahākāruṇika śābara. Next, one should enter the samādhi-wisdom of the immeasurable mind of joy.
With a pure mind, one universally contemplates all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth;
they are originally pure.
Just as a lotus flower is unstained by adventitious dust and is pure by nature,
through the power of the merit I have cultivated by means of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Having observed in this way, one should immediately recite the mantra of the Samādhi of Great Joy:
Oṃ śrī-dharmodgata-sphara. Next, one should enter the wisdom of the samādhi of the immeasurable mind of equanimity.
With a mind of equanimity, one universally takes as objects all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth,
who are all free from "I" and "mine," and free from the aggregates, sense bases, and elements.
Furthermore, being free from the grasper and the grasped,
they are equal with respect to all phenomena,
because the mind is fundamentally unarisen and its nature and characteristics are empty.
"By the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Having contemplated thus:
Then he recited the mantra of the Great Equanimity Samādhi:
Oṃ māhāvaiśravaṇa-sphara. The practitioner, by cultivating the meditative concentration of the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*), recites the mantras of the four immeasurable minds.
In the future, all various demonic activities, karmic obstructions, and difficulties of humans and devas will be entirely extinguished;
immeasurable accumulations of merit will suddenly gather within their bodies,
and their minds will become supple, disciplined, and capable of sovereign mastery.
The practitioner of yoga should not cling to external purity.
Constantly wash the body and mind with the water of the ultimate nature of intrinsic purity.
Recite the purification mantra three times in accordance with the correct principle.
The mantra is:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’haṃ. As it is taught in the Vajraśekhara-yoga-sūtra.
With the vajra bodhicitta of body, speech, and mind as the precursor,
and a purified mind as one's bath,
one who practices yoga for the sake of the benefit and happiness [of others]—
Then, take the unguent and apply it;
join the two hands in *añjali* at the heart and immediately form the *samaya-mudrā* of the Tathāgata family.
Like an unfurled lotus, join the palms;
then place the *jñāna-mudrā* (wisdom finger) upon the upper joint of the *vīrya-mudrā* (effort finger),
with the *dhyāna-mudrā* (meditation finger) and the *prajñā-mudrā* (wisdom finger) each resting against the side of the *vīrya-mudrā*.
Having formed the mudrā,
recite the mantra and enter into yogic visualization,
contemplating that all Tathāgatas pervade the entirety of space.
"May you grant me your blessing.
Furthermore, one should visualize immeasurable rays of light streaming forth from the mudrā,
illuminating and touching all sentient beings without exception.
May one swiftly realize the equality of true suchness (*tathatā*).
By means of this Buddha-samaya-mudrā, may one swiftly realize yoga.
May all sentient beings attain ultimate great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*).
Then he recited the mantra:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām oṃ tathāgatodbhavāya svāhā*. By reciting this mantra and forming the mudrā with focused intention, [the rite was performed].
One becomes equal to all Tathāgatas;
one shall obtain the thirty-two marks of perfection, including the invisible crown protuberance (*uṣṇīṣa*), and the three bodies (*trikāya*) will be perfected.
With this mudrā, place it upon the crown of the head.
Disperse as you please.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family.
Then, join the palms like a lotus bud and place them before your heart.
The *dāna* and *prajñā* fingers are extended upward together;
the remaining six fingers are spread out and bent like an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Having formed the mudrā, recite the mantra.
Entering the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) of the yoga of profound great compassion,
may Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, who fills the realm of space together with immeasurable holders of lotuses,
grant his blessing upon me.
Again, one gives rise to this contemplation:
from the seal, immeasurable rays of light flow forth,
illuminating and touching the seeds of defilement within the fundamental ālayavijñāna of sentient beings in the six realms of existence.
One attains the objectless great compassion that is equal toward oneself and others,
swiftly realizes the illusion-like samādhi,
and manifests various bodies according to the types of beings within the six realms of existence.
Possessing the four unhindered analytical knowledges and the sixty-four kinds of Brahma-voices,
he instantaneously responds to all sentient beings, leading them to the path of Buddhahood.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo kamalāpāṇaye oṃ padmanābhāya svāhā.* By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra for empowerment, [the rite is accomplished].
One becomes equal to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and shall attain the ten stages, the ten masteries, and the three types of mind-made bodies.
With this mudrā, one should release it over one's own mouth.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family:
with the two hands back-to-back, interlace the *tarjanī* (index) and *madhyamā* (middle) fingers with the *anāmikā* (ring) and *kaniṣṭhikā* (pinky) fingers respectively.
Once the mudrā is formed, recite the mantra.
Entering the meditative observation of the Bodhicitta-samādhi,
the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi pervades the entire realm of space,
together with an assembly of the horse-headed Hayagrīva and immeasurable wrathful deities.
I pray that you grant me your empowerment. Furthermore,
visualize immeasurable light radiating from the mudrā,
illuminating and touching all sentient beings— those in the uncertain destinies, those in the realm of ordinary worldlings, and those following the two vehicles.
One will swiftly attain great enlightenment.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇām oṃ vajrunābhaya bha va bha ho*. By reciting this mantra, forming the mudrā, and focusing the mind, one achieves this.
Before long, you shall attain the vajra body, speech, and mind of Vajrasattva,
and be able to expound the wheel of commands of the Secret Teachings,
thereby accomplishing the *siddhis* of superior, middling, and inferior grades for all sentient beings without exception.
One will swiftly and suddenly realize siddhi;
for this reason, one should release this mudrā before one's own heart.
Again, he reflects:
"In all world-systems without exception,
there are immeasurable and boundless sentient beings."
Although they have generated the mind of unsurpassed bodhicitta and have accumulated the provisions of merit and wisdom,
they lack the sublime Dharma empowered by the skillful means and wisdom of yoga.
When those who have fallen away from their roots of virtue find themselves vulnerable to the influence of Māras,
how can one lead each and every sentient being into the wheel of liberation?
For the sake of each and every sentient being.
He proclaims the subtle Mahāyāna of the three secrets yoga,
which swiftly and instantaneously yields the supreme siddhi fruits of both the mundane and supramundane realms;
thus he generates such a mind.
Thus one accomplishes the donning of the great vow-armor.
Next, one should form the supreme mudrā of Vajrapāṇi:
with both hands in the inner-bind (*vajrabandha*), extend the thumbs and ring fingers together.
Bend the two fingers of the *jñāna-bala* (wisdom-power) twice like a hook,
so that they rest against the backs of the first joints of the *kṣānti-praṇidhāna* (patience-vow) fingers,
forming the shape of a three-pronged vajra.
With both meditative concentration and wisdom extended,
one proceeds directly alongside patience and aspiration.
The mantra says:

*Namo samantabuddhānām oṃ vajra-ghaṇṭi-pratīccha svāhā.* With this mudrā, seal the five locations—the forehead, the left and right shoulders, the heart, and the throat—and release it over the crown of the head.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra while maintaining focused attention,
one immediately becomes clad in the vajra armor,
possessing a majestic brilliance equal to that of the Vajra-vidyārāja.
Innumerable and boundless messengers of the Vajra family stand as his guardians;
no obstacles, difficulties, or sentient beings with unwholesome minds are able to harm him,
from the upper reaches of the realm of space down to the limits of the wind-circle below.
All those who dwell in the sky or on the earth,
including the lower classes of vināyakas and others,
shall all give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and be unable to create obstacles for the bodhisattva who practices the true mantra-observances.
Next, one should bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vajracakra and recite the mantra.
By doing so, those who enter the maṇḍala receive the three types of bodhisattva vows that are unobstructed throughout the three periods of time.
By entering the maṇḍala, one becomes fully endowed with the samaya and unconditioned prohibitions (avijñapti-śīla) equal in number to the atoms within the worlds of the atoms of ten buddha-fields.
Consequently, whether through bending or stretching, bowing or looking up, speaking or exhaling, or the arising of thought and movement of mind, [one remains in accordance with these precepts].
If one has forgotten or neglected the bodhicitta and regressed from the roots of virtue,
by reciting and maintaining this seal-mantra through its sublime skillful means and focused mental engagement,
one can eliminate transgressions and faults.
The samaya becomes even more radiant than before;
because it purifies body, speech, and mind,
one thereby accomplishes entry into all maṇḍalas and attains the samaya of empowerment.
Then one should form the mudrā:
with the two hands, the fingers are interlaced within;
the two index fingers are extended straight and held side by side.
The fingers of the patience (kṣānti) and vow (praṇidhāna) mudrās are entwined and advanced with force at the initial joint;
each touches the tip of the other,
while the dhyāna and wisdom fingers are both extended straight.
Recite the mantra seven times with focused attention.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namo strīyadvikāya nāma tathāgatāya | am vīra vīra mahākrodhavajra sata sata sarati sarati trātrā trātrā vidhama triḥ prajñe trāme ti siddhagiri traṃ svāhā.* While reciting this mantra, perform the following visualization:
May all sentient beings within the three realms, the six destinies, throughout the entirety of space and the pervasive dharma-realm,
swiftly enter the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu and become equal to the Great Bodhisattva Vajrasattva.
Next, bind the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā (*vajra-añjali-mudrā*).
With the ten fingers of both hands, cross them so that the right presses against the left; thus it is formed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-jvali. By forming the vajra-palms mudrā, one swiftly attains fulfillment in the ten pāramitās.
One attains the ten masteries.
Next, form the Vajrabandha mudrā:
with the previous mudrā, interlace the ten fingers outwardly and clench them into fists; thus it is accomplished.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-maṇḍala-yoga. By binding the vajra-bond seal, the practitioner swiftly attains the fulfillment of the ten stages (bhūmis).
Next, bind the Vajra-bind mudrā for crushing the ten kinds of obstacles.
As with the previous vajra-bind,
perform three strikes with the mudrā upon the heart center, and it is accomplished.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-manda-traṭ. By forming this mudrā, one is able to destroy the ten kinds of afflictive obstructions within the mind.
Then, manifest and bring forth the vajras of body, speech,
and mind. Next, form the Vajra-Universal-Entry mudrā,
as in the previous Vajra-Bandha mudrā.
Bend the dhyāna and prajñā fingers into the palms;
each grasps the precept finger and places it upon the heart.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrāveśa. By binding this mudrā,
the yogin’s body becomes the three secrets of the vajra.
All shall be brought into compliant submission and sustained by empowerment without dispersal.
Next, bind the Vajramuṣṭi-samaya-mudrā,
as previously described for the Vajrabandha-vyāpaka-mudrā.
The power of progress is fulfilled when meditative concentration and wisdom are joined;
thus it is accomplished.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajramuṣṭi vaṃ. [Then] bind the vajra-fist samaya-mudrā.
The vajras of body, speech, and mind are unified as one;
the practitioner of yoga will swiftly attain all accomplishments.
Next, bind the samaya-mudrā.
As before, with the vajra-bind, straighten the thumbs and ring fingers so they touch; this completes [the mudrā].
Recite the mantra once.
The mantra is:
Oṃ samayastvaṃ. Then one should visualize oneself as being identical to Vajrasattva, abiding within a lunar disc, and further visualize Vajrasattva.
It appears before one like a reflection in a mirror;
it is equal to the body and no different from it.
By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra while maintaining meditative visualization, one attains union.
One immediately attains mastery over all mudrās.
Next, one binds the Great Samaya-Truth Mudrā:
with both hands, form the vajra-bind.
Join the *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers, bending them into the palms with their tips touching.
Straighten and join the *dāna*, *prajñā*, *dhyāna*, and *jñāna* fingers.
Touch the tips of the *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers to the heart center.
The mantra is:
Oṃ samayahuḥ sūtasa tvaṃ yojaya. By forming this mudrā, one awakens the Vajrasattva within the body of the yogin.
Through the empowerment of majestic spiritual power,
the practitioner swiftly attains the body of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Next, one binds the Lotus Samaya Mudrā.
As before, with the vajra-bind,
join the thumbs and wisdom-fingers (tarjanīs) vertically together and place them above the mouth.
Recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajrapadma-samaya-stvaṃ. The practitioner of yoga should contemplate thus:
"Now this body of mine is identical to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara."
Visualize holding a lotus flower at the heart with the left hand,
while the right hand makes the gesture of a blossoming flower;
dwell clearly and distinctly within a perfect lunar disc.

positioned on both sides of the *kṣānti* and *vara* fingers in the shape of a three-pronged vajra.
With the power of meditative concentration and wisdom applied to the side,
rotate the right-turning mudrā three times and recite the mantra three times.
To protect the boundary outside the fire enclosure, one should recite the mantra:
Oṃ śaṅkari mahāsamayaṃ svāhā. By means of the empowerment of this mudrā and mantra, [the protection is established].
As stated in the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya Sūtra* concerning the Golden Wheel-Turning King and others:
if there is anyone who recites and maintains the *Uṣṇīṣarāja* and other *uṣṇīṣa* mantras,
then within five hundred *yojanas*, those who practice the mantras of other sections [will be overcome].
Please consider this: even if the Noble One does not descend or grant siddhi,
it is due to the majestic power of the Sovereign of the Single-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa that he is brought under control.
If this great boundary is thus bound,
even those nearby who maintain the recitation of the Wheel-Turning King will be unable to obstruct it or seize its power.
All other mantras held shall quickly attain accomplishment.
Next, offer arghya water.
With both hands, hold the arghya vessel.
One should offer the water for the face while reciting the mantra seven times,
visualizing that it bathes the feet of all the noble assembly.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ gaganasamavasaraṇa svāhā.* When the practitioner offers the arghya water, [he recites this].
Regarding whatever matter one desires in one's heart,
one should immediately make a vow and declare:
"O Noble One, may the siddhi I seek be swiftly accomplished."
Next, form the mudrā of the Flower Offering Seat: join the two hands in the lotus-petal *añjali* gesture, positioned at the heart like an unfurled lotus.
With the thumbs and middle fingers of each hand, pinch the nails of the ring fingers and little fingers to form the pedestal.
Having completed the remaining visualizations according to the vajra-mudrā,
one should visualize the mudrā as a vajra-lotus.
Furthermore, one should imagine that immeasurable vajra-lotus seats flow forth from the mudrā.
Offer this to the principal deity and the assembly of noble ones.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrakamala svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra, [the offering is perfected].
Once the principal deity and the retinue have each truly received their seats, next,
form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padma-ullāsa-līlā: join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture.
When meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) are held upright and slightly opened,
and [the visualization] is settled upon the heart, it is accomplished.
The practitioner of yoga (*yogin*) visualizes himself as the Bodhisattva Hevajra.
Visualize that from within your heart, immeasurable Bodhisattvas of Joyful Play (Ratimādana) stream forth to make offerings to the Principal Deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
This is the mantra of the Lotus Joyful Play.
Oṃ praṇamya ralakṣirāgaya mahādevīrāgapūjāyā hūṃ svāhā. Because one performs this mudrā and recites this mantra as an offering.
Before long, they will attain the stage of a Tathāgata;
dwelling in the perfection of the Dharma, they will abide in happiness in this very life and realize unsurpassed enlightenment.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmamālā: with the aforementioned mudrā, extend the arms forward until they are level with one’s own forehead.
Visualize that from the forehead, immeasurable Bodhisattvas Padmamālā stream forth.
Make offerings to the principal deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra for the Lotus Garland (*padmamālā*) is as follows:
*Oṃ padmamāle viśuddhe prasādaka bhūrja karmaya hūṃ svāhā*. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one makes the offering.
One will obtain the perfection of the primary and secondary marks and shall become the Dharma King of the three realms.
Next, bind the Lotus Song-Praising Bodhisattva Seal: take the aforementioned seal and lower it until it reaches the level of the navel.
Joining the palms in the lotus gesture, slowly and gradually raise them until they reach the mouth;
then, using the mudrā, let it flow downward from the mouth forward.
Visualize that immeasurable lotuses emerge from the mouth, singing praises to the Bodhisattva.
Make offerings to the principal deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra for the Lotus Song of Praise is as follows:
Oṃ padmanarteśvari gīta-nartita-prayoga-samaye hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, one makes the offering.
Before long, you shall be endowed with the sixty-four kinds of Brahma-voices and the four types of unimpeded eloquence, and be able to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma throughout immeasurable worlds.
Next, form the Lotus Dance Bodhisattva mudrā: make a lotus-fist with each of the two hands.
First, they rotate each other at the right side of the chest like a dance;
next, they likewise rotate each other at the left side of the chest in a dancing posture;
then, they rotate as before at the right cheek and then the left cheek.
Recite the mantra without interruption.
At the end, join the palms in the lotus gesture and place them upon the crown of the head.
Visualize that from the crown, immeasurable lotuses and dancing bodhisattvas stream forth.
Make offerings to the principal deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
The mantra for the Lotus Dance is:
Oṃ padmanṛtye sarvabhuja-pravartana māye hūṃ svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra while making offerings, [the rite is accomplished].
One shall attain three kinds of swift, mind-made bodies (*manomayakāya*), through which one may,
in a single instant, perform miraculous displays throughout immeasurable worlds to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
Extensively perform the Buddha-activities.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Lotus Incense-Burning Bodhisattva:
join the two hands in the lotus-palms gesture.
Place both hands together, palms facing downward, and scatter the fingers.
Visualize that from this mudrā, clouds and oceans of sublime fragrance flow forth,
pervading the entire Dharma-realm and making universal offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
The mantra for burning incense with a lotus is as follows:
Oṃ padma-dhūpa-bhūja-samaye praharaṇāya padma-kurāna-īte mahā-gaṇike padma-rati hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, one makes an offering.
One attains the Tathāgata’s unimpeded vajra-liberation wisdom.
Next, one forms the Lotus Flower Offering Bodhisattva mudrā: join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture.
Directing the hands upward as if scattering flowers,
one should visualize various sublime celestial flowers flowing forth from the mudrā to universally make offerings to the ocean-like assembly of all Tathāgatas.
The mantra for the offering of lotus flowers is:
Oṃ puṣpa-prajñe padma-vāsini mahā-śrīye padma-kula-pratīhāri sarva-ratna-saṃdhāya hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra while making the offering, [the rite is accomplished].
One obtains a body of infinite enjoyment, adorned with a hundred merits.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmapradīpa: join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture, and visualize the thumbs and wisdom-fingers (middle fingers) joined together while held upright.
From the seal, immeasurable lights of mani-jewels flow forth,
universally illuminating all buddha-fields.
The mantra of the Lotus Lamp-Candle is as follows:
Oṃ nibhābhūrja-samaye bhaṇma-kūla-śūṇḍari mahānuttīya-ru-kañjasanajñāya bhaṇma-sarvasvati hūṃ. Because one performs the offering by forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra.
One attains the Tathāgata’s five pure eyes.
Next, form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Padmagandhahasti: join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture at the heart, then spread the fingers apart in the manner of applying fragrant unguent.
Visualize that from within the mudrā, clouds and oceans of scented unguents flow forth,
making universal offerings to the ocean-like assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
Then, recite the Lotus Scented Unguent Mantra as follows:
Oṃ khadhāpujya samaye mahāpadmakuṇḍali jvala kuṇḍali sarvakarmāṇi me padmasiddhi hūṃ. Because one offers by forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, [the deity is pleased].
One attains the fivefold Dharma-body consisting of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
Next, one forms the seal of universal offering to make offerings to the primary deity and the assembly of noble ones.
Interlace the first fingers of both hands at the ten points;
having formed the mudrā, recite the mantra while contemplating that oceans of various offering clouds flow forth from the mudrā.
The exquisite celestial music, song, dance, and amusements;
the exquisite celestial garments, food, drink, and lamps;
the argha-water, auspicious jars, kalpavṛkṣa trees, precious banners, parasols, and various other such jewels.
All objects of enjoyment possessed by humans and devas,
and the various diverse articles of offering,
such as the articles of offering described in the Mahāyāna sūtras.
Pervading all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm,
before each of the assemblies of Buddhas in every ocean-like gathering within all lands as numerous as atoms,
there are authentic offerings.
Recite the mantra:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ svāhā khaṃ udāgate saparikhedaṃ gaganakaṃ svāhā*. Then recite the hymn of praise to the tutelary deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).

Oṃ vajradharma sūtradhāra tvaṃ | Vajrapadma susvadhākara | Ājñeśvara svavajrājña | Vajreṇa tvaṃ namo satyena hili hili | [End of] the Upper Scroll of the Ritual for Recitation, the *Ārya-harivajra-mahācaṇḍarāja-siddha-mahāprabhāva-pūjā-japa-vidhi*.
[Beginning of] the Lower Scroll of the Chapter on the Ritual for Recitation and Offering, the *Ārya-harivajra-mahācaṇḍarāja-siddha-mahāprabhāva-pūjā-japa-vidhi-dharmapada*.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra, of Great Wisdom, Śramaṇa of Daixingshan Monastery, Imperial Advancer and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, by Imperial Decree.
Next, [he] forms the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Dānapāramitā: the right hand with the palm facing upward.
Curl the fingers of the *kṣānti-pāramitā* and join them with the *dhyāna-pāramitā*,
while extending all the remaining fingers.
Then, recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ vāg-vati jñānādhipate visarjaya svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
One immediately extinguishes the seeds of stinginess accumulated over immeasurable kalpas and attains the three kinds of merit from giving:
namely, the gift of material goods, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of the Dharma.
Thus, the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) is fulfilled;
in this very life, one obtains abundant wealth and resources,
and the mind attains mastery.
One’s lifespan shall be long and far-reaching.
Next, form the Bodhisattva Seal of the Precept Pāramitā: interlace the two hands with palms facing inward and extend the *dhyāna* (ring) and *jñāna* (middle) fingers straight upward.
Recite the mantra as follows:
Recite the mantra three times while forming this mudrā: *Oṃ śīladharini bhagavati hūṃ haḥ*.
Immediately, the seeds of transgressions against the precepts accumulated over immeasurable kalpas will be extinguished.
One attains the threefold merit of ethical discipline:
namely, the morality of restraint, the morality of gathering virtuous dharmas, and the morality of benefiting sentient beings.
This is the perfection of the pāramitā of ethical discipline.
They constantly adorn the actions of body, speech, and mind with the categories of ethical discipline (*śīla*).
As for all violations of the four grave prohibitions,
or the eight *pārājika* offenses committed by bhikṣuṇīs—
All shall be completely purified;
in the future, they will attain rebirth in accordance with their vows.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva of the Perfection of Forbearance (Kṣāntipāramitā).
Following the previous seal of the precept-pāramitā,
join the fingers of effort (vīrya) together like a needle;
the dhyāna and wisdom (prajñā) fingers stand side by side.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ vagvati kṣaṃtī dāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ. While forming this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Thus, one extinguishes the seeds of immeasurable kalpas of anger and affliction,
and attains the merits of the three kinds of patience:
namely, the patience of enduring harm from enemies, the patience of accepting suffering, and the patience of discerning the Dharma.
Thus, the perfection of patience is fulfilled;
his appearance is dignified and handsome, bringing joy to those who behold him;
free from mutual hatred or envy, all come to draw near to him in affection.
With even deeper resolve, one recollects the transformation.

Next, bind the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Perfection of Vigor (vīrya-pāramitā). Following the previous mudrā of the Perfection of Forbearance (kṣānti-pāramitā), it is formed by bending and opening the fingers with vigor.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vīryakari hūṃ vīraṇa svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, the seeds of karma consisting of indolence and laziness accumulated over immeasurable kalpas are extinguished,
and one attains three kinds of diligence:
namely, the diligence of donning the armor, the diligence of gathering virtuous dharmas, and the diligence of bringing benefit and happiness to sentient beings.
Thus, the perfection of diligence is fulfilled;
body and mind are peaceful and blissful, free from all illness and devoid of suffering.
Such are his supramundane merits, wisdom, and aspirations.
All shall be accomplished.
Next, bind the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Dhyānapāramitā:
sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), with the left hand palm upward upon the lap.
Place the right hand palm-upward upon the left hand,
with the nails of the two fingers of wisdom and meditation touching one another.
Then recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ vagavati sarvabādhāharaṇi mahānāthade hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Thereby, one extinguishes the seeds of distraction accumulated over immeasurable eons and attains the three kinds of meditative concentration:
namely, the meditative concentration of abiding, the meditative concentration of manifestation, and the meditative concentration of accomplishing activities.
Thus, the dhyāna-pāramitā is perfected;
body and mind become light and agile,
and the supernatural powers one cultivates are swiftly accomplished.
No māras shall be able to invade or disturb them;
all karmic obstructions will be entirely extinguished.
Next, form the Bodhisattva Seal of Prajñāpāramitā: Extend the five fingers of the left hand flatly and place it facing upward below the heart;
cover the left hand with the right hand, palm facing down.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ śrī-sūrata-vijaye svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, the seeds of ignorance and delusion accumulated over immeasurable kalpas are extinguished,
and one attains three kinds of wisdom: namely,
non-conceptual wisdom regarding the emptiness of persons, non-conceptual wisdom regarding the emptiness of phenomena, and non-conceptual wisdom regarding the emptiness of both.
Then the perfection of prajñāpāramitā will be fulfilled;
one will attain keen intelligence and wisdom,
and realize the mundane and supramundane dharmas.

Having extensively mastered the profound principles of the five sciences (*pañcavidyā*), he next binds the Bodhisattva Seal of the Perfection of Skillful Means (*upāyapāramitā*): with the left hand, representing wisdom (*prajñā*) and the direction of space, he grasps the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*);
with the right hand, representing generosity (*dāna*) and ethical discipline (*śīla*), he grasps the perfection of meditation (*dhyānapāramitā*).
The two hands are joined palm-to-palm;
the thumbs and ring fingers are turned inward and held straight up like needles;
the index and middle fingers are extended flat and pressed together.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ mahā-maitrī-citte svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, they extinguish the seeds of karma from immeasurable eons that lack skillful means,
and they attain two kinds of skill in means:
namely, the skill in means of dedication and the skill in means of delivering sentient beings.
This constitutes the perfection of the *upāya-pāramitā*.
By practicing the six mundane *pāramitās* and through union with this seal-mantra yoga, [one attains fulfillment].
With little exertion, their meritorious deeds and karmic accomplishments become vast and manifold;
they swiftly attain fulfillment,
as all these constitute the ultimate, most excellent provisions for unsurpassed bodhi.
Next, form the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Perfection of Vow:
Hold the five fingers of the left hand straight and upright, with the palm facing outward in the gesture of granting fearlessness.
Then recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ karuṇi he he saṃyukte. Recite this mantra three times while forming this mudrā;
it will immediately extinguish the seeds of evil vows and karma accumulated over immeasurable kalpas.
One attains two kinds of supreme aspirations:
namely, the aspiration to seek unsurpassed enlightenment and the aspiration to bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings,
as well as the perfection of the pāramitās.
From the initial generation of the mind of enlightenment until the attainment of Buddhahood,
all the supreme worldly aspirations sought during that interval shall be fully realized.
Next, bind the Bodhisattva mudrā of the Perfection of Power (*vīrya-pāramitā*). It is modeled after the previous mudrā of the Perfection of Morality (*śīla-pāramitā*);
however, the *dhyāna*, *jñāna*, *vīrya*, *bala*, *kṣānti*, and *praṇidhi* fingers are all held upright with their tips joined together.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ namo nirmokṣadhāte hūṃ ha ha ha hūṃ jayā. While forming this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, they extinguish the seeds of inferior mental karma pertaining to both worldly and world-transcending states over immeasurable eons,
and obtain two kinds of power:
namely, the power of analytical discernment and the power of cultivation.
Regarding the various remedial dharmas,
one subdues and attains the severance of all afflictions and the obstacles of delusion;
this is the definitive resolve at the time of cultivating the path.
One cannot be moved by any celestial Māras or evil friends;
one attains non-retrogression.
Next, form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Prajñāpāramitā: interlace the two hands with the palms facing outward and form fists.
The *dāna* and *prajñā* fingers are held upright and slightly interlaced;
the tips of the *vajra* fingers are bent inward and pressed together to form a circle.
The *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers are held upright with their tips joined.
Then recite the mantra:
Oṃ mama-mañji-kāriṇi hūṃ svāhā. Having bound this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.
Immediately, one extinguishes the seeds of innate self-grasping and innate grasping at phenomena that have coexisted for immeasurable eons,
and attains two kinds of wisdom of enjoyment:
namely, the wisdom of enjoying the dharma-pleasure of what is grasped.
The wisdom that accomplishes sentient beings;
it abandons the two kinds of obscurations,
namely the afflictive obscuration and the cognitive obscuration.

They realize that all phenomena are like an illusion, like a mirage, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like the moon in water, like a magical transformation, like Indra’s net, and like space.
Before long, he will fulfill the ten stages and abide in the Dharma-Cloud stage (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), becoming a great Dharma Master.
Next, form the *brahmadāra* (Brahmin Youth) mudrā: interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Forming fists with the tips of the thumbs and forefingers pressed together to form circles, with both the middle and ring fingers extended upright, the mantra is recited as follows:
*Tadyathā* (1) *buddhe buddhe* (2) *subuddhe* (3) *indrabuddhe* (4) *mame śukalane* (5) *pramocatu svāhā*. By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra three times, [the purpose is accomplished].
None of the vināyakas shall find an opportunity;
if there are wicked people who cause obstacles against one who is innocent,
imagine those evil persons beneath the feet of the practitioner.
If one recites the mantra twenty-one times,
all obstacles will completely dissipate;
those who harbor ill will toward one another will be unable to create hindrances.
Furthermore, it can assist the power of the principal deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
Next, form the seal of the Brahmā-kumāra: interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward;
join the two index fingers (*tarjanī*) together and extend them upright, leaving them slightly apart.
When meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) are established simultaneously, the mantra is recited as follows:

*tadyathā* (1) *sara-pāra* (2) *sārya-viśaya* (3) *vajra-kūla* (3) *pā* (4) *bhaspada* (5) *kaccid-uṣi* (6) *svāhā*. By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra three times, [the rite is accomplished].
It can subdue and expel all evil māras;
furthermore, no calamities from thieves or enemies can cause harm,
and it can assist the primary deity.
Next, form the mudrā of the One-Tufted Rākṣasa Youth. Following the previous Vairocana mudrā, join the tips of the thumbs and index fingers together like a needle; this completes it.
The mantra is as follows:
*Tadyathā | oṃ | śvetadhyā | śvetasajja | sattva | mahākāruṇika | svāhā.* Because one recites this mantra three times while forming this mudrā, [the following occurs].
Expel all demons, spirits, and deities belonging to the four directions who might obstruct the power of the *iṣṭadevatā*.
Next, bind the seal of the youth Aparājita, following the previous seal of the single-topknot *rākṣasa*.
Bend the forefinger slightly like a lotus petal and it is accomplished.
The mantra is:
Oṃ riṣṭi-lukāviśaye amogha-paśya mahā-kurudha rājñe ṛtaye aparājita hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra three times, [the rite is completed].
It can expel all demons, evil spirits, and ghosts, whether in the heavens or in space;
it ensures that all undertakings are accomplished without hindrance or difficulty,
and it can augment the power of the *iṣṭadevatā*.
All siddhis will be accomplished according to the practitioner’s wishes.
Next, bind the seal of the Nanda Nāga King: join the two thumbs together and hold them upright.
Twist the tips of the two little fingers together.
Hold both hands upright and pressed against each other,
with the two index fingers twisted together.
On the two thumbs and the two little fingers;
the ring fingers are likewise.
The two middle fingers are on top.
The heads do not quite meet;
the palms touch below, while the fingers move back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ mahāśrīye svāhā. Next, bind the mudrā of the Nāga King Vāsuki: interlace the four fingers, beginning with the index finger, in reverse order.
Turn the hands inward and interlace them.
Bend the left thumb into the space between the index finger and the palm;
extend the right thumb straight inward without bending it.
Join the two wrists together and move the right thumb back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ mahāśveti svāhā. Next, form the mudrā of the Nāga King Takṣaka: join the wrists;
extend the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers.
Bend both heads so they touch each other,
aligning them with the original joint.
Place the two thumbs side by side, pointing upward and touching one another.
Press the sides of the index fingers together;
join the tips of the two little fingers while keeping them upright;
then move the thumbs back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ citan lu tan lu viśaye svāhā. Next, form the seal of the Dragon King Karkoṭaka by joining the wrists.
Extend the two thumbs and the two little fingers straight upward with their tips joined;
keep the remaining fingers straight and extended without touching one another.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bodhi bodhabodhe svāhā. Next, form the seal of the Nāga King Pramoda: with the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands, interlace them with the tips pointing outward.
Join the palms with the right hand placed over the left;
let the fingertips touch the backs of the palms,
and keep the two index fingers side by side.
The thumb is likewise;
it spreads against the index finger and moves back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vātagati svāhā. Next, form the seal of the Naga King Mahāpanna: bend the left thumb toward the palm, then bend its tip away from the thumb by about four or five *aṅgula*.
With the three fingers below the middle finger,
pinch the fingernails together and place the seal horizontally and askew against the heart.
Point the fingers to the right.
The mantra is:
Oṃ śveti jñe svāhā. Next, bind the seal of the Nāga King Śaṅkhapāla: the two ring fingers [are interlaced] left and right.
Place each [finger] separately on the back of the middle fingers.
Join the tips of the two middle fingers together while keeping them upright.
Place the two little fingers and the two thumbs side by side against one another.
Bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch each other,
each pressing down on the tip of the thumb;
the index fingers should be aligned level with the second joint.
Move the index fingers back and forth. The mantra is:
Oṃ vīrikūṭi bharati kārāpa svāhā. Next, form the mudrā of the Nāga King Kūlika: bend the two ring fingers into the palm, with the right pressing down upon the left.
The two little fingers and the two middle fingers are each held upright and joined together;
the two index fingers are bent and each placed against the lower joint of its respective middle finger.
Bend both thumbs and place them against the sides of the lower joints of the index fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bhagavati vīrikūti prāṇeti prabhāvati svāhā. Having tied the seals of these eight great nāga kings and recited the mantra three times for each, [proceed].
Together with immeasurable hosts of nāgas, they surround and assist the power of the principal deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
The practitioner of yoga accomplishes all activities with sovereign majesty.
Next, bind the mudrā of Maheśvara: form a fist with the right hand and place it at the right hip.
The five fingers of the left hand are held straight up and touching one another.
The earth and water fingers (the little finger and ring finger) are bent at their middle joints.
The fire, wind, and space fingers (the middle, index, and thumb) are each slightly separated from one another; thus it is formed.
The mudrā is held upright with the fingers pointing outward. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ iśāne svāhā*. Next, bind the mudrā of Śakra: the right hand is as before.
The five fingers of the left hand are held upright and touching one another.

The earth and water fingers (the ring finger and little finger) are bent at their middle joints, with the wind finger (the middle finger) placed against the back of the fire finger (the index finger).
The space finger (the thumb) is bent at its middle joint.
The mantra is: Oṃ indrāya svāhā.
Next, form the seal of the Fire Deity (Agni): clench the left hand into a fist and place it at the waist;
extend the five fingers of the right hand straight upward, touching one another.
Bend the empty [fingers] and place them within the palms;
bend the middle joints of the wind [fingers].
The mantra is as follows:

Oṃ agnaye svāhā. Next, form the seal of Yama: first join the palms; bend the middle joints of the two earth-fingers (the thumbs) so their backs touch, and likewise bend the two wind-fingers (the index fingers) so their backs touch.
To form [the seal], press the second joints of the wind-fingers (middle fingers) with both thumbs.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jñāne svāhā. Next, perform the Rākṣasa-devatā mudrā: form a fist with the right hand and place it at the waist.
The five fingers of the left hand are held straight up and pressed together;
bend the middle joints at the earth and water positions,
and by pressing the tips against the earth and water nails, the seal is formed.
The mantra is:
Oṃ dharitrīye svāhā. Next, form the seal of Varuṇa: the right hand is as before;
the left hand forms a fist with the thumb not entering the palm.
Hold the wind-finger (the little finger) straight up.
Slightly bend the middle joint and it is complete.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vāruṇāya svāhā. Next is the mudrā of the Wind Deity (*Vāyu*). The right hand is as before;
the five fingers of the left hand are held straight upward, and the middle joints of the [thumb and index finger] are bent, thereby forming it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vaye ve svāhā. Next, form the seal of Vaiśravaṇa: first join the palms with the ten fingers interlaced, the tips pointing inward.
The two water fingers stand upright with their tips touching.
The two wind fingers stand upright and are slightly bent.
The left space finger enters the right palm and presses down upon the left fire nail.
Insert the right thumb through the left thumbhole from behind and place it within the left palm.
Press down upon the right fire-armour.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vaiśravaṇāya svāhā. Next, form the seal of Brahmā: make a fist with the right hand and place it at the waist;
extend the five fingers of the left hand upward, slightly bending them.
When its height slightly exceeds the shoulders, one should form the visualization of a lotus.
The mantra is: Oṃ mālāmaṇe svāhā.
Next, perform the earth-goddess mudrā (*pṛthivī-devatā-mudrā*): first join the palms and touch the tips of the four fingers below the wind-fingers (the little fingers) together.
Open wide in front.
Place the two *śūnyatā* [syllables] on either side of the wind.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ pṛthivīye svāhā. Next, bind the seal of the Sun Deity (Sūrya): it is not different from the previous seal of the Earth Deity (Pṛthivī), except that the two thumbs are joined.
Each [finger] rests upon the lower joint of the water [element]. The mantra is:
Oṃ ānityāya svāhā. Next, form the seal of Candradeva: it is like the previously described seal of Brahmā.
Simply form the mudrā of the fist with the appearance of a pure white moon within it.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jvala nātha svāhā. By forming the seals of the twelve Heavenly Kings and reciting this mantra, [the purpose is accomplished].
The practitioner of yoga performs all activities with sovereign power and majesty.
Furthermore, there is the Noble Lord Hayagrīva, the Wrathful King.
The mudrā and mantra for the Great Protective Body Boundary are now explained:
Interlace the three fingers from the middle finger downward with the palms facing outward;
join the backs of the hands together with the palms pressed flat.
The two index fingers are held upright at a distance of about five *aṅgula* from each other;
the two thumbs are placed side by side and touching,
with their first joints bent so as not to touch the index fingers.
Move the index fingers back and forth. The mantra is:
Oṃ pravicāṣṭa vajraśvara rucaye svāhā. The Noble Lord Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King, further taught the mantra of the Dharma-body mudrā.
With the index fingers of both hands,
cross the remaining three fingers outward;
join the palms so that the tips of the fingers each touch the back of the hand.
Join the two little fingers together by placing them side-by-side and pointing upward;
likewise, join the two thumbs together and bend them in a wrathful manner,
moving the thumbs back and forth.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ oṃ jana jana mata mata khada khada hana hṛdaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the Noble Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Great Dharma Heart-Seal (*mahādharmacittamudrā*) is taught:
with the two hands, interlace the four fingers from the index fingers downward outwardly;
place the tips of the fingers against the backs of the hands and join the palms.
Place the two thumbs together.
Bend each one at a single joint so that it does not touch the index finger; move the thumbs back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Homage to the Noble Hayagrīva, the King of Fierce Wrath.
Furthermore, the mantra for the Great Dharma-Head Seal is as follows:
it accords with the previous protection-of-the-body seal,
with the only modification being that the tips of the two index fingers are pressed together.
Bend each [finger] so that two large joints protrude,
with the small tips pointing forward.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samanta buddhānām. Tadyathā: cakari bhuḥ, cakara cakhari bhuḥ, cakara padmamukhari bhuḥ, amogha khāsiro kiṃviḥ, paraśanāgacchadu, svāhā. The Noble Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.

It follows the previous head seal,
with the sole modification that the two index fingers are raised and their tips joined together.
Place the middle fingers of both hands in front of the index fingers with their tips touching.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ śrīraja hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the Noble Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.
Furthermore, the mantra of the Dharma-mouth seal is as follows:
Again, interlace the two fingers within the palms,
and extend the two middle fingers straight upward so that their tips touch one another.
Extend both thumbs upright;
with the right index finger, press the tip of the right thumb,
while the left index finger is held upright and slightly curved.
On the side of the middle finger, the mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ | oṃ tittirururu kurudaya svāhā*. This is the Noble Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.

It follows the previous seal,
with the sole modification that the two middle fingers are extended straight upward with their tips touching.

First, grasp the back of the right ring finger with the left little finger,

The mantra is as follows:

Furthermore, the mudrā and mantra for consuming all obstacles are explained: With the left hand, extend all five fingers upward;
with the right hand, point downward and join the tips of the middle, ring, and thumb fingers together.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ haṃ hūṃ khaṇḍa-pañja-sphoṭaya svāhā*. This is the Noble Hayagrīva, the Greatly Majestic Wrathful King.
Furthermore, he taught the mantra and the sharp-edged sword seal for severing all hindrances:
with both hands of concentration and wisdom,
form the vajra-fist.
The honest and upright one fans the fire;
space sustains the earth and water;
samādhi serves as the hilt for the hand.
Taking Prajñā as a sword,
the sword of wisdom enters, abides, and emerges—
all within the scabbard of samādhi.
This is the majestic mudrā and ritual conduct of the Venerable Hayagrīva for severing all obstacles:
the hand of concentration rests upon the heart,
while the hand of wisdom revolves universally.
One should know that the objects touched serve to remove defilements;
by means of this counter-clockwise rotation, the ritual of warding off obstacles is accomplished.
If one is binding the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions,
one should cause them all to follow a clockwise rotation;
this applies to all other ritual activities as well.
To extinguish evil and purify all obstacles,
one should likewise act in this way,
corresponding to each respective category.

their forms are exceedingly large, fierce, and possess great power.
Their bodies were blue and red, with disheveled hair hanging down on both sides;
each wore a crimson *kāṣāya* robe,
and tiger skins were draped around their front, back, waist, and flanks.
On both hands and wrists of Dao Bu,
there were precious bracelets;
only those of Bo Luo Duo Mo were missing.
The left and right hands hold a single sharp spear.
Vairocana holds a battle-axe in his left and right hands.
As for the Single-Hair Rākṣasa:
his right hand holds a vajra staff,
and his left hand holds a lasso.
As for Aparājitā:
her right hand holds a sharp sword,
and her left hand holds a vajra.
These four great messengers each possess sovereign majesty and power;
each protects King Vīrabhadra,
and each kneels upon a gong-shaped stone.
His entire body is enveloped in great flames,
blazing and radiant like the light of the sun;
he has a most violent and malevolent form.
He is able to subdue all non-Buddhists and celestial Māras, and to settle all evil yakṣas and malevolent spirits,
causing them all to take refuge in the Buddha and the Dharma,
because they recollect the Great Majestic Wrathful Honored One.
The four great youths constantly followed and protected him,
never leaving his side, as if they were not separate from their own bodies,
as if guarding the pupils of their eyes, and as if protecting their own lives.
Because one maintains the messenger,
one is immediately able to penetrate the affairs of the three periods of time.
If there is a person who has not yet recited the mantra, [they cannot do so].
As soon as one recalls the Wrathful King,
the two guardians who protect the mantra-reciter,
and the four great youths, they shall guard him day and night, never departing from his side.
Furthermore, I shall now describe the images of the eight great nāga kings according to the semblance dharma (pratirūpaka-dharma).
These eight great nāga kings are of one essence and without distinction;
they have the heads of dragons and the bodies of snakes, with flames blazing from their entire bodies.
When there is thunder and lightning,
or when great hailstones fall and heavy rain pours down,
one should invoke the names of the eight dragon kings.
All thunder and lightning can be suppressed so that they immediately dissipate.
Furthermore, if the great earth should tremble and shake in every direction,
and mountains, rivers, and rocky cliffs should shatter and break apart.
A violent and fierce wind suddenly blows,
felling all the great trees; even so,
when such various calamities and hardships arise.
For those sentient beings who are terrified and unsettled,
one should invoke the names of these eight dragon kings;
this will be able to suppress all earthquakes and malignant winds.
The five grains will be abundant and the myriad people will live in peace and happiness.
Wind and rain will follow their proper seasons, the land will be secure and tranquil,
and there will be no further calamities or disasters.
How much more so for the practitioner’s own body;
if there should be any calamity, it shall not find a place here,
and Māra shall gain no advantage.
One shall swiftly realize great enlightenment and before long become a Buddha.
This concludes the teaching on the Dharma-gate of the Messenger of the Noble Hayagrīva, the Great Majestic Wrathful King.
